reuse.why: The new getExpectedScheduleAmount builds on getScheduledAmount and the server callers are routed through it, but it re-derives the 7.5% tolerance inline instead of calling the existing getApproxNumberThreshold in shared/rules.ts.

duplication.why: It removes the inline null/number/range ternaries in app.ts and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, but duplicates the approximate-tolerance formula and leaves schedule-template.ts deciding which ops go to the helper.

placement.why: The rule sits in shared/schedules.ts beside getScheduledAmount, and the server modules only consume it.

scope.why: Only the amount resolution call sites, one type field and focused tests change.

maintainability.why: Two exported helpers with overlapping meaning (getScheduledAmount vs getExpectedScheduleAmount) invite the wrong choice, and the tolerance now lives in two places that can drift apart from transaction matching.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount computes Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) itself instead of calling getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.ts

disguised_duplication.where: The tolerance in getExpectedScheduleAmount restates getApproxNumberThreshold's formula inline; schedule-template.ts keeps its own op dispatch (isbetween || isapprox ? helper : value) around a helper that already handles every op.

one_place.where: The server paths (app.ts, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, forecast-schedules.ts, api-models.ts, schedule-template.ts) use getExpectedScheduleAmount, but schedule-template.ts still pre-selects ops itself, the tolerance is defined separately from getApproxNumberThreshold, and client consumers (Balance.tsx, SchedulesTable, mobile lists, useScheduleEdit) still call getScheduledAmount without the approximate rule.
